traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Basellaceae: leaves opposite or alternate; leaves simple; veins pinnate or palmate; stipules absent; leaf rosettes basal or none; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes monoecious; ovary superior; floral cup present; stems herbaceous; flowers in racemes, in spikes or in panicles; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals or tepals; parts of each whorl 5; stamens 5; carpels 3. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.perennation.note: Family file kept: FNA vol. 4 (read 2026-10-19) mentions the tubers of Ullucus and the tubers or starchy rhizomes of Anredera.

traits.growth_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): vines (herbs outside the flora), perennial, succulent, mucilaginous, glabrous; FOC vol. 5: herbaceous vines or twining herbs, usually fleshy.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves alternate; FOC vol. 5: simple, alternate.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves simple.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade margins entire (toothed outside the flora); FOC: entire.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): plants glabrous; FOC: glabrous.

traits.stipules.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stipules absent.

traits.rosette.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): twining vines with leafy stems; neither FNA vol. 4 nor FOC vol. 5 describes a rosette. DELTA's basal state kept as rarely.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): succulent herbaceous vines.

traits.sexual_system.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers usually bisexual; FOC: bisexual. Family file kept.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): spikes, racemes or panicles; FNA: racemose (spicate or paniculate outside the flora).

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers actinomorphic, small.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals 2, petals (4-)5(-13) basally connate, but some authors take the 2 sepals for bracts and the petals for sepals; FOC vol. 5 follows that view: 2 persistent bracteoles and 5 perianth segments. Family file's either-way reading kept.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): perianth segments 5; stamens 5.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens (4-)5(-9), on the petals, basally connate; FOC: 5, opposite the segments.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pistil 3-carpellate, unilocular, 1 ovule; styles 3.

traits.ovary_position.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): ovary superior.

traits.hypanthium.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): perianth hypogynous, hypanthium present.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits utricles wrapped in a dry or fleshy perianth; FOC: a utricle, dry or fleshy. The vocabulary has no utricle, so achene (a dry one-seeded fruit).

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Basellaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): perianth segments persistent in fruit, the bracteoles too, often surrounding the utricle.
